1.word_for_word: trayastriṃśe — in the thirty-third chapter; tataḥ gopī-maṇḍalī-madhya-gaḥ hariḥ — then Hari, situated among the circle of gopīs; priyāḥ tāḥ ramayām āsa — delighted those beloved women; hradinī-vana-kelibhiḥ — with sports in the river and forest; tat tadā aṅga he rājan — ‘then, O King’; yad vā tasya bhagavataḥ aṅgena — or: by the body/limbs of Bhagavān; upacitāḥ samṛddhāḥ āśiṣaḥ yāsām — whose blessings/fortunes were increased by contact with his limbs; alternative: tāsām gopīnām aṅgaiḥ upacitā āśiṣaḥ yasya — or, Kṛṣṇa's own joy/fortune was increased through the gopīs' limbs
1.translation: In the thirty-third chapter Hari, standing within the circle of gopīs, delights his beloved companions through play in the forest and water. ‘Then, O King’ is one reading of the opening. Alternatively, the wording may describe the gopīs as those whose great fortune was increased through contact with Bhagavān's body and limbs; another possible construction makes Kṛṣṇa's own festive joy appear augmented by the limbs of the gopīs.

2.word_for_word: rāsa-krīḍām — the rāsa sport; rāsaḥ nāma bahu-nartakī-yuktaḥ nṛtya-viśeṣaḥ — rāsa is a particular form of dance involving many female dancers; anyonyam ābaddhāḥ saṃgrathitāḥ bāhavaḥ — with arms linked together; definition cited: nartakīnām maṇḍalī-bhūya nartanam — dancers forming a circle and dancing while mutually holding hands/necks
2.translation: ‘Rāsa’ is a particular kind of dance performed by a group of women with their arms linked together. Śrīdhara cites a technical definition: when female dancers form a circle, holding one another in linked formation, and dance, that is called rāsa.

3-4.word_for_word: tat-sāhityam abhinayena darśayati — the text dramatically shows Kṛṣṇa's simultaneous presence with them; rāsa-utsave — in the rāsa festival; akṣara-avaruddha-praviṣṭena — he entered into every interval; kaṇṭhe gṛhītānām ubhayataḥ āliṅgitānām — each gopī found herself embraced at the neck from both sides; sarvāḥ striyaḥ sva-nikaṭam mām eva āśliṣṭavān iti manyeran — so that every woman thought ‘he has embraced me alone beside me’; dvayoḥ dvayoḥ madhye praviṣṭena — he entered between every pair; nanu ekasya katham tathā praveśaḥ — how can one person enter all those places; yoga-īśvareṇa — because he is Lord of Yoga; acintya-śaktinā — by inconceivable power; tat-kṣaṇam eva — at that very moment; autsukya-vyāpta-manasām sa-strīkāṇām devānām — the gods with their wives, minds filled with eagerness; vimāna-śataiḥ saṅkulam nabhaḥ — the sky became crowded with hundreds of celestial vehicles
3-4.translation: The narration dramatizes Kṛṣṇa's simultaneous presence throughout the rāsa circle. He entered every interval between pairs of gopīs so that each one experienced him immediately beside herself, embracing her, and each thought, ‘Kṛṣṇa is with me alone.’ How could one person occupy all those positions? Because he is Yogeśvara, the Lord of Yoga, possessing inconceivable power. At that same moment the gods and their wives, filled with eager wonder, crowded the sky in hundreds of celestial vehicles.

5.word_for_word: tat tasya bhagavataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya — of that Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa; amalam nirmalam yaśaḥ — spotless, pure glory; jaguḥ — they sang
5.translation: The celestial singers sang the spotless and pure glory of Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

6.word_for_word: sa-priyāṇām — of the gopīs together with their beloved Kṛṣṇa; kṛṣṇa-sahitānām — accompanied by Kṛṣṇa; tumulaḥ — loud, dense, mingled
6.translation: The sound was ‘tumula’—a rich, loud intermingling produced by the gopīs together with their beloved Kṛṣṇa.

7.word_for_word: mahā-marakataḥ nīla-maṇiḥ iva — like a great blue-green emerald; haimānām maṇīnām madhye madhye — among golden jewels; tābhiḥ svarṇa-varṇābhiḥ āśliṣṭābhiḥ śuśubhe — embraced by the golden-complexioned gopīs he shone; gopī-dṛṣṭi-abhiprāyeṇa — or from the gopīs' point of view; vinā madhya-pada-āvṛttim eka-vacanam — the singular construction is used without repeating the middle term
7.translation: Kṛṣṇa shone among the golden-complexioned gopīs like a great dark emerald set amid golden jewels. Śrīdhara also notes a grammatical way of reading the singular expression from the viewpoint of each individual gopī.

8.word_for_word: yathā sa tābhiḥ śuśubhe tathā tā api tena virejuḥ — just as Kṛṣṇa shone through them, they shone through him; pāda-nyāsaiḥ — by placements of the feet; bhuja-vidhutibhiḥ — movements of the arms; bhajyamānaiḥ madhyaiḥ — bending waists; caladbhiḥ kucaiḥ ca paṭaiḥ ca — moving breasts and garments; gaṇḍa-lolaiḥ — ornaments/curls moving against the cheeks; svidyat-mukhyaḥ — faces beaded with perspiration; kabareṣu raśanāsu ca granthayaḥ dṛḍhā yāsām — whose hair knots and girdles remained bound, or alternatively whose knots became loosened; nānā-mūrtiḥ kṛṣṇaḥ megha-cakram iva — Kṛṣṇa in many manifestations like a mass of clouds; tāḥ bahu-vidhāḥ taḍitaḥ iva — the gopīs like many streaks of lightning; svedaḥ tuṣāraḥ iva — perspiration like mist; gītam garjitam iva — song like thunder
8.translation: As Kṛṣṇa was beautified by the gopīs, they in turn shone through him. Their footwork, sweeping arms, bending waists, moving breasts and garments, swinging ornaments and perspiring faces filled the dance with motion. Śrīdhara gives two possibilities for the wording about hair and girdles: their knots may be described as firm, or as loosening in the dance. He then develops the image: Kṛṣṇa's many manifestations resemble a circle of dark rainclouds, the many gopīs resemble flashes of lightning, their perspiration is like fine mist, and their song like thunder.

9.word_for_word: nṛtyamānāḥ — dancing; rakta-kaṇṭhyaḥ — whose voices/throats were colored; nānā-rāgaiḥ anurañjita-kaṇṭhyaḥ — voices colored by different musical rāgas; kṛṣṇasya abhimarśena saṃsparśena muditāḥ — delighted by Kṛṣṇa's touch; idam viśvam — this whole universe
9.translation: They danced with their voices colored by many musical rāgas and were filled with joy by Kṛṣṇa's touch. Their singing seemed to fill the entire universe.

10.word_for_word: mukundena saha svara-jātīḥ — melodic classes sung together with Mukunda; ṣaḍja-ādi-svara-ālāpa-gatīḥ — movements of tones beginning with ṣaḍja; amiśritāḥ — unmixed; kṛṣṇa-unnītābhiḥ asaṅkīrṇāḥ — kept distinct from those raised by Kṛṣṇa; prīyamāṇena saṃmānitā — honored by pleased Kṛṣṇa; tat-jāti-unnayanam eva dhruvam — she elevated the melodic form into a dhruva; dhruvākhyaṃ tāla-viśeṣam kṛtvā — using the rhythmic form called dhruva
10.translation: One gopī sang distinct melodic patterns with Mukunda, moving through tones beginning with ṣaḍja without merely merging into Kṛṣṇa's own line. Pleased, Kṛṣṇa honored her. Śrīdhara explains that her elaboration of the melodic form was performed with the particular rhythmic pattern called dhruva.

11.word_for_word: nṛtya-gīta-ādinā śrī-kṛṣṇa-saṃmānitānām — of those honored by Śrī Kṛṣṇa through dance and song; ati-prīti-vilasitam vṛttam — the behavior manifesting their intense joy; ślathanti valayāni mallikāḥ ca yasyāḥ — one whose bracelets and jasmine garland were loosening
11.translation: Śuka next describes signs of the gopīs' intense joy as Kṛṣṇa honored their dancing and singing. One gopī's bracelets and jasmine garland loosened as she danced.

12.word_for_word: utpalasya saurabham yasya — possessing the fragrance of a blue lotus; tam bāhum — that arm
12.translation: Kṛṣṇa's arm is described as fragrant like a blue lotus.

13.word_for_word: nāṭyena nṛtyena vikṣiptayoḥ cañcalayoḥ kuṇḍalayoḥ tviṣā — by the brilliance of earrings made to swing by the dance; maṇḍitam gaṇḍam kapolam — her cheek was adorned; sva-gaṇḍe sandadhatyāḥ saṃyojayantyāḥ — as she pressed that cheek against Kṛṣṇa; alternate grammatical note — the combined brilliance of moving earrings and the cheek's natural luster ornaments it
13.translation: As the dance made her earrings swing, their brilliance joined the natural glow of one gopī's cheek. She pressed that luminous cheek against Kṛṣṇa. The source includes a grammatical note explaining the compound as the combined radiance of the moving earrings and cheek.

14.word_for_word: kūjatī nūpure mekhalā ca yasyāḥ — one whose anklets and girdle were sounding
14.translation: Another gopī's anklets and jeweled girdle rang out as she danced.

15.word_for_word: evam anyā api gopyaḥ — in this way the other gopīs also; yathā-yatham — each according to her own manner; nānā-vibhramaiḥ vijahruḥ — sported with many graceful gestures
15.translation: In this way all the other gopīs too sported with Kṛṣṇa, each displaying her own distinctive graceful gestures.

16.word_for_word: vādakeṣu gāyakeṣu gandharva-kinnara-ādiṣu rasa-āveśena muhyatsu — while celestial instrumentalists and singers such as Gandharvas and Kinnaras became overwhelmed by rasa; anyām eva vādya-ādi-sampattim darśayan — the dance itself produced another, self-sufficient musical ensemble; karṇa-utpalaiḥ — with lotuses at their ears; ālaka-viṭaṅkaiḥ alaka-alaṅkṛtaiḥ kapolaiḥ — cheeks ornamented by hanging curls; gharmaiḥ ca vaktreṣu śrīḥ — beauty from perspiration upon their faces; ghoṣāḥ kiṅkiṇyaḥ — tinkling bells; valaya-nūpura-ghoṣaiḥ vādyaiḥ — bracelets and anklets serving as instruments; sva-keśebhyaḥ srastāḥ srajaḥ — garlands falling from their hair; tāla-gati-santuṣṭāḥ keśāḥ sa-śiraḥ-kampam pādeṣu puṣpa-vṛṣṭim iva akurvan — poetic fancy: their hair, pleased by the rhythm, shook down flowers at their feet like a shower of blossoms; bhagavatā saha nanṛtuḥ — they danced with Bhagavān; bhramarā eva gāyakāḥ yasyām rāsa-sabhāyām — in an assembly where the bees themselves seemed to be singers
16.translation: Even the Gandharva, Kinnara and other celestial musicians became stunned by the rasa, while the dance itself generated its own complete music. Lotuses adorned the gopīs' ears, curls framed their cheeks, and perspiration brightened their faces. Their girdle-bells, bracelets and anklets became instruments. Garlands slipped from their hair; Śrīdhara poetically imagines their hair, delighted by the rhythm and shaken with their heads, showering flowers upon their own feet. Thus they danced with Bhagavān in a rāsa assembly where even the bees seemed to serve as singers.

17.word_for_word: yathā gopyaḥ nānā-vibhramaiḥ bhagavatā saha vijahruḥ — as the gopīs sported with Bhagavān through many gestures; evam bhagavān api sva-vilāsaiḥ tābhiḥ saha reme — Bhagavān likewise sported with them through his own līlā; tad-vilāsaiḥ anabhibhūtasya — while himself remaining unconquered by those charms; yathā arbhakaḥ sva-pratibimbaiḥ — like a child playing with its own reflections; svīyam eva sarva-kalā-kauśalam saugandhya-lāvaṇya-mādhurya-ādi ca tāsu sañcārya — imparting to them his own arts, fragrance, beauty, sweetness and other qualities; tābhiḥ saha reme — he played with them
17.translation: As the gopīs sported with Bhagavān through countless graceful gestures, Bhagavān reciprocated through his own līlā while remaining completely unconquered by their charms. The comparison is to a child playing with its own reflections: Kṛṣṇa had imparted to the gopīs their arts, fragrance, beauty, sweetness and every excellence, and then delighted in play with these manifestations of his own power.

18.word_for_word: bhagavad-vilāsaiḥ ākulāḥ — overwhelmed by Bhagavān's play; tasya aṅga-saṅgena prakṛṣṭā mut prītiḥ — intense joy arising from contact with his body; tayā ākulāni avaśāni indriyāṇi — their senses became overwhelmed and no longer under control; viślatha-bandhān keśa-ādīn añjasā prativyoḍhum — they could not immediately restore their loosened hair and clothing; visrastā mālā ābharaṇāni ca — garlands and ornaments had slipped
18.translation: The gopīs themselves were overwhelmed by Bhagavān's playful affection. Contact with his body produced such intense joy that their senses became powerless; they could not at once restore loosened hair, garlands, garments and ornaments to their former arrangement.

19.word_for_word: na kevalam tā eva ākula-indriyāḥ — not only the gopīs became overwhelmed; devyaḥ api — celestial women did too; kṛṣṇa-vikrīḍitam — seeing Kṛṣṇa's play; śaśāṅkaḥ ca — even the moon; śaśāṅkena vismitena gatau vismṛtāyām — the astonished moon forgot its movement; tataḥ prāktanāḥ sarve grahāḥ tatra tatra eva tasthuḥ — the other planets likewise remained fixed in their places; ati-dīrghāsu rātriṣu yathā-sukham vijahruḥ — thus the night became extraordinarily long for their play
19.translation: Not only the gopīs were overwhelmed; the celestial women were as well. Even the moon, astonished by Kṛṣṇa's sport, forgot to move. The planets consequently seemed to remain fixed, and the night stretched to extraordinary length, giving Kṛṣṇa and the gopīs ample time for their play.

20.word_for_word: pratyekam tābhiḥ prārthanāt — because each gopī had individually prayed to Kātyāyanī; nanda-gopa-sutam patim me kuru — ‘make Nanda's son my husband’; bhagavatā api tathaiva pratiśrutatvāt — and because Bhagavān had promised accordingly; yāta abalā vrajam siddhā mayā imā raṃsyatha kṣapāḥ — ‘return to Vraja, your vow is successful; you will enjoy with me on these nights’; tāvantam ātmānam kṛtvā — he manifested as many forms of himself as there were gopīs; reme — and sported with each; yāvatīḥ yāvatyaḥ — as many as they were
20.translation: Each gopī had individually prayed to Kātyāyanī, ‘May Nanda's son become my husband,’ and Kṛṣṇa had personally promised, ‘Your vow is successful; on these coming nights you will sport with me.’ To fulfill each individual prayer exactly, he manifested as many forms of himself as there were gopīs and danced with each one.

21.word_for_word: kṛpā-atiśayam āha — the verse expresses the extraordinary degree of his grace; tāsām iti — beginning ‘for them’
21.translation: The next verse emphasizes the extraordinary abundance of Kṛṣṇa's grace toward the gopīs.

22.word_for_word: ati-hṛṣṭānām gopīnām caritam — the behavior of the greatly delighted gopīs; sphuratām svarṇa-kuṇḍalānām kuntalānām ca — flashing golden earrings and moving locks; tviṣā gaṇḍeṣu śrīḥ — their brilliance beautified the cheeks; sudhitena amṛtāyitena hāsa-sahitena nirīkṣaṇena — with nectar-like smiling glances; ṛṣabhasya patyuḥ kṛṣṇasya mānam dadhatyaḥ — honoring Kṛṣṇa, their foremost lord; pūjām kurvatyaḥ — worshiping him; tat-karmāṇi jaguḥ — they sang of his deeds; tasya kararuhaiḥ nakhaiḥ sparśena pramodaḥ yāsām — delighted by the touch of his fingernails
22.translation: The delighted gopīs' golden earrings flashed beside moving curls, illuminating their cheeks. With nectar-like smiling glances they honored Kṛṣṇa, their supreme beloved, and worshiped him by singing his deeds, rejoicing in the touch of his fingernails.

23.word_for_word: atha jala-kelim āha — now the water-sport is described; tāsām aṅga-saṅgena ghṛṣṭā sammarditā yā srak — Kṛṣṇa's garland rubbed against their bodies; kuṅkuma-rañjitāyāḥ — therefore colored with the kuṅkuma from their breasts; sambandhibhiḥ gandharva-pālibhiḥ — surrounded by rows of bees like Gandharva chiefs; gāyantaḥ alayaḥ — bees humming as though singing; taiḥ anudrutaḥ — followed by them; sa kṛṣṇaḥ vāḥ udakam āviśat — Kṛṣṇa entered the water; bhinna-setuḥ vidārita-vapraḥ — breaking through boundaries like a river that bursts its bank; svayam ca atikrānta-loka-veda-maryādaḥ — himself transcending ordinary social and scriptural boundaries
23.translation: The narration turns to their water-play. Kṛṣṇa's garland had rubbed against the gopīs' bodies and become colored with the kuṅkuma from their breasts. Bees followed its fragrance, humming like celestial singers, as Kṛṣṇa entered the water with the gopīs. Śrīdhara likens him to a river that breaks through its embankment: in this divine līlā he stands beyond the ordinary boundaries of worldly and Vedic convention.

24.word_for_word: sva-ratiḥ — whose delight is in himself; ātmārāmaḥ api — though entirely self-delighting; atra gopī-maṇḍale ambhasi vā — he nevertheless sports here among the gopīs or in the water
24.translation: Even here in the water among the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa remains ‘sva-rati’ and ‘ātmārāma’—one whose fulfillment and delight are intrinsically in himself.

25.word_for_word: sthala-jala-krīḍe darśite — after describing play on land and in water; vana-krīḍām darśayati — forest play is now described; yamunāyā upavane — in a grove beside the Yamunā; jala-sthala-prasūnānām gandhaḥ yasmin anilena — filled with a breeze carrying fragrance from flowers of water and land; jūṣṭāni diśām taṭāni antāḥ — the quarters and banks were pervaded by it; bhṛṅgāṇām pramadānām ca gaṇaiḥ āvṛtaḥ — Kṛṣṇa was surrounded by swarms of bees and groups of women
25.translation: Having described play on the riverbank and in the water, Śuka turns to forest play in a Yamunā grove. The breeze carried the mingled fragrance of aquatic and terrestrial flowers through the surrounding quarters, while Kṛṣṇa moved amid swarms of bees and groups of gopīs.

26.word_for_word: rāsa-krīḍām nigamayati — Śuka concludes the rāsa play; sa kṛṣṇaḥ satya-saṅkalpaḥ — Kṛṣṇa, whose will is unfailing; anurāgi-strī-kadamba-sthaḥ — situated among the loving assembly of women; sarvā niśāḥ sīṣevē — enjoyed those nights; śarat-kāvya-kathā-rasāśrayāḥ — nights embodying all the poetic rasa associated with autumn; alternative: śṛṅgāra-rasa-āśrayāḥ śaradi prasiddhāḥ kāvyeṣu yāḥ kathāḥ tāḥ sīṣevē — he enacted all the celebrated autumnal narratives of erotic rasa described by poets; ātmany eva avaruddhaḥ saurataḥ carama-dhātuḥ — his generative/sexual power remained restrained within himself; na tu skhalitaḥ — it was not discharged; kāma-jaya-uktiḥ — this explicitly declares his conquest of desire; source note — all autumnal poetic possibilities that poets of every place and time could describe are said to be encompassed by the līlā
26.translation: Śuka now concludes the rāsa festival. Kṛṣṇa, whose will is always fulfilled, spent those autumn nights among the loving gopīs, embodying all the poetic rasa traditionally associated with the season. Śrīdhara then emphasizes the theological point already announced at the beginning of the five chapters: Kṛṣṇa's erotic potency remained completely ‘restrained within himself’ and was not discharged. This phrase expressly proclaims his victory over kāma, not subjection to it. The accompanying note says that the līlā encompasses all the autumnal poetic possibilities that poets of every place and time could ever describe.

28.word_for_word: pratīpam — contrary; pratikūla-adharmam — behavior opposed to ordinary dharma; ācarat — he performed it; na ca idam adharma-mātram kalanja-bhakṣaṇa-ādivat — this is not merely a minor prohibited act like eating forbidden food; mahā-sāhasam — it appears an extreme transgression; para-dāra-abhimarśanam — contact with others' wives
28.translation: Parīkṣit's objection is serious: Kṛṣṇa's conduct appears opposed to ordinary dharma, and not merely as a minor prohibition such as eating forbidden food; touching others' wives would ordinarily be regarded as a major transgression.

29.word_for_word: āpta-kāmasya na ayam adharmaḥ iti cet — if one answers that no sin attaches to one whose desires are already fully satisfied; yadi evam kāma-abhāvāt — then because he has no personal desire; ninditam kena abhiprāyeṇa kṛtavān — with what purpose did he enact something ordinarily condemned; iti pṛcchati — this is the force of Parīkṣit's question
29.translation: Suppose one says that no adharma can attach to Kṛṣṇa because he is āpta-kāma, completely fulfilled and devoid of personal desire. Parīkṣit's further question is then: precisely because he had no desire to satisfy, for what purpose did he enact behavior that is ordinarily condemned?

30.word_for_word: parameśvare kaimutika-nyāyena parihartum — to answer concerning the Supreme Lord by an a-fortiori argument; sāmānyataḥ mahatām vṛttam āha — Śuka first states the general rule concerning great beings; dharma-vyatikramaḥ — apparent transgression of ordinary dharma; sāhasam ca dṛṣṭam prajāpati-indra-soma-viśvāmitra-ādīnām — such extraordinary acts are seen in Prajāpati, Indra, Soma, Viśvāmitra and others; tejasvinām doṣāya na bhavati — in beings of exceptional spiritual power such acts do not necessarily produce fault
30.translation: To answer the case of the Supreme Lord by an a-fortiori argument, Śuka first states a more general principle: extraordinary departures from ordinary rules are found even in powerful figures such as Prajāpati, Indra, Soma and Viśvāmitra, and such acts do not necessarily produce the same fault in spiritually powerful beings that they would in ordinary persons.

31.word_for_word: yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhaḥ iti nyāyena anyaḥ api kuryāt iti āśaṅkya — objection: according to ‘whatever a great person does, others follow,’ might ordinary people imitate this; na etat iti — Śuka answers ‘not so’; anīśvaraḥ — one without such sovereign power; deha-ādi-paratantraḥ — an ordinary person dependent upon body and conditions; yathā rudra-vyatiriktaḥ viṣam bhakṣayan — like anyone other than Rudra attempting to drink poison
31.translation: An ordinary person may not appeal to the maxim ‘whatever the greatest person does, others should imitate.’ Someone without the corresponding divine power, bound by body and conditions, would destroy himself by imitation—just as a person other than Rudra would die by attempting to drink poison as Rudra did.

32.word_for_word: katham tarhi sad-ācārasya prāmāṇyam — how then can the conduct of great persons serve as authority; īśvarāṇām vacaḥ satyam — their explicit teaching is authoritative; tat uktam ācaret eva — one should follow what they instruct; ācaritam tu kvacit satyam — their conduct is authoritative only in suitable cases; sva-vacaḥ-yuktam — behavior consistent with their own teachings; teṣām vacasā yad yad yuktam aviruddham — whatever in their conduct does not conflict with their teaching; tat tad eva ācaret — that alone should be imitated
32.translation: How, then, does the conduct of great persons function as an example? Their explicit instruction is authoritative and should be followed. Their personal conduct is exemplary only where it accords with their teaching and does not contradict the principles they themselves enjoin. Those compatible actions may be imitated; extraordinary sovereign acts may not.

33.word_for_word: nanu tarhi te api kim evam sāhasam ācaranti — why do liberated great beings ever perform such extraordinary acts; kuśala iti — the verse beginning ‘the skillful’ answers; prārabdha-karma-kṣapaṇa-mātram eva teṣām kṛtyam — for such realized beings, their remaining activity serves only to exhaust already-begun karma; na anyat — nothing else remains to be attained
33.translation: If one asks why realized great persons ever perform unusual acts at all, Śrīdhara answers that for such beings nothing remains to be gained; their embodied activity serves only the exhaustion of the prārabdha that maintains the body.

34.word_for_word: prastutam āha — Śuka returns to Kṛṣṇa specifically; kim uta iti — ‘how much more, then...’; kuśala-akuśala-anvayaḥ na vidyate — no connection with merit or demerit exists for him; kim punaḥ vaktavyam — what more need be said
34.translation: Śuka then returns from the general case to Kṛṣṇa: if even realized beings can stand beyond ordinary karmic consequences, how much more the Supreme Lord, to whom no connection with merit or demerit can attach at all?

35.word_for_word: yasya pāda-paṅkaja-parāgasya niṣevaṇena tṛptāḥ — those satisfied through serving the pollen-like dust of his lotus feet; yad vā yasya pāda-paṅkaja-parāge niṣevā yeṣām — or those whose constant service is fixed upon his foot-dust; te ca tṛptāḥ — such devotees are fulfilled; jñāninaḥ ca na nahyamānāḥ — and knowers are not bound; bandhanam aprāptavantaḥ — they do not become subject to bondage
35.translation: Those who serve the dust of Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet become fulfilled and free of bondage; the same is true of knowers of reality. If those who depend upon him can be released from karmic bondage, bondage cannot coherently be attributed to the Lord himself.

36.word_for_word: para-dāratvam gopīnām aṅgīkṛtya parihṛtam — the objection has so far been answered even granting the premise that the gopīs were others' wives; idānīm bhagavataḥ sarva-antaryāmiṇaḥ — now a deeper answer is given from Bhagavān's being the indwelling Self of all; para-dāra-sevā nāma na kācit — for the universal inner Self there is ultimately no category ‘another man's wife’; yaḥ antaḥ carati adhyakṣaḥ buddhi-ādi-sākṣī — he who moves within all as the overseer and witness of mind and intelligence; sa eva krīḍanena deha-bhāk — that same Lord merely assumes embodied appearance for līlā; na tu asmad-ādi-tulyaḥ — he is not an ordinary embodied individual like us; yena doṣaḥ syāt — therefore the ordinary fault cannot apply
36.translation: The preceding answers provisionally granted the claim that the gopīs were ‘other men's wives.’ Śrīdhara now gives a more fundamental response: Bhagavān is the indwelling Self of every being. He is the overseer and witness within the minds of the gopīs, their husbands and all creatures. His visible body is assumed for līlā and is not conditioned embodiment like ours. Thus the ordinary possessive category ‘another man's wife,’ and the fault based on it, cannot ultimately be applied to the universal inner Self.

37.word_for_word: nanu āpta-kāmasya nindite kutaḥ pravṛttiḥ — why would one completely fulfilled enact something outwardly condemned; anugrahāya iti — ‘for grace’; śṛṅgāra-rasa-ākṛṣṭa-cetasaḥ ati-bahirmukhān api — even persons whose minds are extremely externalized and attracted primarily by erotic rasa; sva-parān kartum — to make such people his own devotees
37.translation: Why, then, would the self-fulfilled Lord enact a līlā that superficially resembles condemned conduct? ‘For grace.’ Śrīdhara's answer is that even people whose minds are extremely externalized and attracted mainly by romantic or erotic rasa can be drawn through this līlā toward Kṛṣṇa and made his own.

38.word_for_word: nanu anye api bhinna-ācārāḥ sva-ceṣṭitam evam eva iti vadanti — objection: other immoral people may claim the same justification for their own behavior; na asūyan iti — the verse excludes that; evam-bhūta-aiśvarya-abhāve — where such divine sovereignty is absent; tathā kurvantaḥ pāpāḥ jñeyāḥ — persons behaving similarly are to be understood as sinful
38.translation: If ordinary transgressors claim that their own conduct is the same as Kṛṣṇa's, the answer is explicit: without Kṛṣṇa's divine sovereignty and nature, similar behavior is simply sinful. The līlā cannot be used to excuse ordinary misconduct.

39.word_for_word: brahma-rātre — when the night reached the brahma period; brāhme muhūrte — at the brāhma-muhūrta before dawn; upāvṛtte prāpte — when that time arrived
39.translation: The rāsa night concluded as the brāhma-muhūrta, the sacred period before dawn, arrived.

40.word_for_word: bhagavataḥ kāma-vijaya-rūpa-rāsa-krīḍā-śravaṇa-ādeḥ — hearing and recounting Bhagavān's rāsa līlā, whose true nature is his conquest of desire; kāma-vijayam eva phalam — yields conquest of desire as its own fruit; acireṇa dhīraḥ san — becoming steady before long; hṛd-rogam kāmam — lust, the disease of the heart; āśu apahinoti parityajati — quickly removes and abandons it; alternative: kāmam yathā-iṣṭam āśu bhaktim labdhvā — or, obtaining devotion quickly and abundantly according to one's longing; kāma-ādi-sarva-hṛd-rogam acireṇa hinoti — one soon destroys lust and every other disease of the heart
40.translation: Śrīdhara closes the five rāsa chapters by stating their fruit. Because Bhagavān's rāsa līlā is, in its theological meaning, a manifestation of his conquest of desire, faithfully hearing and recounting it leads the hearer toward the same conquest. One soon becomes steady and casts off lust, the disease of the heart. Alternatively, the line may mean that by quickly obtaining abundant devotion one soon destroys lust and all other diseases of the heart.
